# Results — Study 621 (Share-Class Spreads)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **BRK.B can
never cost more than 1/1500th of BRK.A** (the one-way A→B conversion is a bound the market
enforces daily), while **GOOG vs GOOGL has no bound at all** — measured on the full daily tape
of both pairs. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete month before the 2026-07-03 run
date; later sessions are sliced off). Fingerprint `145603f5d518`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **split-adjusted** closes (`auto_adjust=True`), 4 tickers, 1996-05-01 → 2026-06-30 (7,589 days) |
| BRK pair | 7,583 overlapping days, 1996-05-09 (B issue) → 2026-06-30; the 2010-01-21 50:1 B split makes the adjusted parity a constant **1,500 B per A** across the whole tape (30 B per A pre-split) |
| GOOG pair | 3,078 overlapping days, 2014-04-03 (class-C distribution) → 2026-06-30; the 2022 20:1 split and the 2024+ dividends hit both classes identically |
| Gap definitions | BRK gap = 1500·B/A − 1 (negative = B cheap); GOOGL voting premium = GOOGL/GOOG − 1 |
| Execution / costs | exactly **one lag**: signal at close *t*, filled at close *t+1*, first return accrues *t+1 → t+2*; costs **2/5/10 bps one-way × NAV per leg** (a class switch = 2 legs); pairs short leg pays **50 bps/yr borrow**; all returns price-only on adjusted closes (neither BRK class has ever paid a dividend; Google's 2024+ dividends are identical on both classes, so they cancel in the ratio) |
| Selection note (Signal axis) | no panel and no survivorship screen — two *named*, still-trading mega-cap pairs chosen because they are the textbook bounded/unbounded dual-class contrast; nothing was searched over |

> **Close-print noise.** BRK-A trades a few hundred times a day at ~$750k a share, so the two
> classes' 4 p.m. prints are non-synchronous — a few bps of apparent "premium" is measurement
> noise, not a violated bound. The bound is judged at the **50–100 bps** level, where prints
> cannot hide.

## 1 — Bound enforcement: does B ever cost more than A/1500?

| B above parity by … | share of days | days |
|---|--:|--:|
| > 0 bps | 35.80% | 2,715 |
| > 10 bps | 18.08% | 1,371 |
| **> 50 bps** | **1.77%** | **134** |
| > 100 bps | 0.24% | 18 |

Worst upward excursion **+194 bps on 2020-03-13** (COVID liquidity chaos); worst downward
**−700 bps on 2009-02-20**. Tail asymmetry beyond ±50 bps: **22.95%** of days below vs
**1.77%** above — a **13.0×** one-way-bound signature. The GOOG pair, with no conversion
bridge, is symmetric: 40.16% of days above +50 bps vs 26.74% below (ratio **0.7×**). The
premium days that do exist cluster in 1996–98 (B's first years), 2008 and March 2020 —
liquidity events, not a failed bound.

## 2 — The structural B discount

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean gap | **−35.5 bps** · **HAC t = −12.53** (NW lags = 10, n = 7,583) |
| median / std | −8.2 bps / 82 bps |
| p1 / p99 | −385.7 bps / **+62.7 bps** |
| min / max | −700 bps / +194 bps |

| era | mean gap | HAC t | days B above parity |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1996–2009 | −55.1 bps | −10.82 | 33.9% |
| 2010–2019 | −7.1 bps | −5.99 | 44.9% |
| 2020–2026 | −37.7 bps | −10.83 | 25.9% |

*(Era boundary = the 2010-01-21 B-share 50:1 split: the "1996–2009" row runs through
2010-01-20, the last pre-split session.)*

The distribution is exactly what a one-way conversion predicts: **capped above** (p99 = +63 bps)
with a **long free tail below** (p1 = −386 bps). The mean B discount is small but decisively
non-zero (HAC t = −12.5), significant in every era.

## 3 — GOOGL voting premium (no bound)

Mean **+51.6 bps**, HAC t = +6.45 (NW lags = 8, n = 3,078); std **149 bps** (vs 82 for the
bounded BRK gap); range **−435 → +531 bps**.

| era | mean premium | HAC t | days GOOGL below GOOG |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2014–2017 | **+237.5 bps** | +28.59 | 0% |
| 2018–2021 | −4.8 bps | −0.65 | 50% |
| 2022–2026 | **−53.9 bps** | −14.74 | **90%** |

The "voting premium" is not a constant near zero — it **changed sign**: +238 bps in 2014–17,
then persistently *negative* since 2022 (the non-voting class rich 90% of days), the well-known
tilt from Alphabet's buybacks concentrating in class C. With no conversion bridge, nothing
forces the spread anywhere.

## 4 — Mean-reversion half-lives

| pair | AR(1) ρ | half-life |
|---|--:|--:|
| BRK gap (bounded, arbitraged) | 0.8566 | **4.5 trading days** |
| GOOG gap (unbounded) | 0.9919 | **85.2 trading days** |

The bound is visible in the dynamics too: the BRK gap snaps back ~19× faster than the free
GOOG spread.

## 5 — Tradability: long-cheap/short-rich pairs trade on the BRK gap

Entry |z| > 1.5 (252-day window), exit |z| < 0.25; dollar-neutral; one execution lag; costs
one-way × NAV per leg; the short leg pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| convention | result |
|---|---|
| *Diagnostic*: fill at the signal's own close print, gross | +8.42%/yr · HAC t = +9.38 (in market 33% of days) |
| **Honest next-close fill, net @ 2 bps** | **+0.21%/yr · HAC t = +0.38** |
| Honest next-close fill, net @ 5 bps | −0.95%/yr · HAC t = −1.69 |
| Honest next-close fill, net @ 10 bps | −2.87%/yr · HAC t = −4.75 |

The entire paper profit lives in the assumption that you transact **at the very prints that
define the signal**. Delay the fill by one close — the only honest convention on close-stamped
data — and the edge is statistically zero at 2 bps and reliably negative at realistic costs.

## 6 — Third axis: has the B-discount ever been a tradable signal for A-holders?

Switch overlay: an A-holder sells A and buys 1,500 B whenever B is ≥ thr cheap, switches back
at parity; excess return vs just holding A, net @ 5 bps one-way × 2 legs per switch.

| convention / threshold | net excess | HAC t | pre-2010 | 2010+ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| *Diagnostic* fill-at-print, thr = 1% | +4.27%/yr | +6.02 | — | — |
| **Honest, thr = 0.5%** | −0.56%/yr | −1.03 | −1.06%/yr (t −0.93) | −0.15%/yr (t −0.39) |
| **Honest, thr = 1%** | +0.14%/yr | +0.28 | +0.13%/yr (t +0.12) | +0.14%/yr (t +0.43) |
| **Honest, thr = 2%** | +0.30%/yr | +0.73 | +0.67%/yr (t +0.74) | −0.01%/yr (t −0.04) |
| **Honest, thr = 3%** | +0.42%/yr | +1.18 | +0.76%/yr (t +0.95) | +0.14%/yr (t +1.00) |

(The 1% diagnostic row uses 158 switches, 23% of days in B.) **In no era and at no threshold**
does the honest version clear even t = 1.2. The apparent +4.3%/yr (t = 6.0) is a fill-at-the-
signal-print artefact: the "discount" you act on is partly the wide, stale BRK-A close itself,
and it is gone by the first close at which you could actually trade. **BUSTED.**

## 7 — Synthetic positive control — the detector is faithful

Deterministic two-class world (seed 621): shared fundamental + AR(1) relative-value gap, with
a planted mean discount and an optional hard one-way bound.

| world | mean gap | HAC t | days > +50 bps | days < −50 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **PLANTED bound + −40 bps discount** | −54.9 bps | **−33.86** | 0.00% | 52.64% |
| **NULL: no bound, zero discount** | −3.1 bps | **−1.50** | 14.40% | 16.98% (asym 1.2×) |

The detector recovers the planted bound (zero upward tail, decisive negative t) and does **not**
manufacture one from a symmetric unbounded null (asym 1.2×, |t| < 2). *(A machinery check only —
never cited in support of the stamps.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The one-way bound is on the tape: B exceeds parity by >50 bps on only
  **1.77%** of days (>100 bps: 0.24%, worst +194 bps in the March-2020 chaos), against a free
  tail to −700 bps — a **13× asymmetry** — and the structural B discount of **−35.5 bps**
  carries **HAC t = −12.5** (significant in every era). The unbounded GOOG pair is the perfect
  control: symmetric excursions (0.7×), an 85-day half-life vs 4.5 for BRK, and a "voting
  premium" that flipped from +238 bps to −54 bps as buybacks tilted to class C. Two named
  mega-cap pairs, no panel, no search — the selection note stands in for survivorship.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** With one honest execution lag the z-score pairs trade nets
  **+0.21%/yr (t = 0.38)** at 2 bps and is negative at 5+ bps; the A-holder switch overlay
  never clears t = 1.2 at any threshold in any era. Add the access walls — one BRK-A share
  ≈ $750k, the conversion privilege is one-way and broker-mediated, and the whole gap averages
  35 bps — and nothing deployable remains. The bound is real *because* conversion arbitrageurs
  enforce it; there is nothing left for you.
- **"Has the B-discount ever been a tradable signal for A-holders?" — BUSTED.** The +4.3%/yr
  (t = 6.0) paper edge exists only if you fill at the signal's own close prints; delayed one
  close, it is +0.1–0.4%/yr at t ≤ 1.2 everywhere, pre-2010 wild-discount era included.
